title: Revised 2035 local food production targets and Singapore Food Story 2
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how the revised 2035 fibre and protein production targets compare with the '30 by 30' targets in total local food production volume, and how the Ministry will ensure they are adequate, sustainable and resilient. Ms He Ting Ru asked why targets are set for fibre and protein, and how Singapore's food security is measured against local farming production.
asked_by: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms He Ting Ru
response: Mr Zaqy Mohamad said the previous '30 by 30' strategy sought to produce 30% of nutritional needs by 2030 and has evolved into Singapore Food Story 2, with local production as one of four pillars alongside import diversification, stockpiling and global partnerships. The revised local production targets are 20% of local consumption of fresh leafy and fruited vegetables, beansprouts and mushrooms, and 30% of eggs and seafood. Meats and alternative protein are excluded, while rice and poultry will be considered under other pillars. Support for farms includes grants, land tenders, lowering production costs, building capability, strengthening input supply resilience and enhancing demand offtake, with more details at the coming Committee of Supply.

key_points.point: The previous "30 by 30" strategy aimed to produce 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: the previous "30 by 30" strategy sought to develop local capability and capacity to produce 30% of our nutritional needs by 2030.

key_points.point: It has evolved into Singapore Food Story 2, focused on overall food resilience.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: This has evolved into the Singapore Food Story 2, which aims to bring about overall food resilience.

key_points.point: Local production is one of four food security pillars, alongside import diversification, stockpiling and global partnerships.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Local production is one of the food security pillars of the Singapore Food Story 2, complemented by three other pillars which are import diversification, stockpiling and global partnerships.

key_points.point: New local production targets are 20% of local consumption of fresh leafy and fruited vegetables, beansprouts and mushrooms, and 30% of eggs and seafood.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: We want to work with our local farms to build up the capability and capacity to supply 20% of our local consumption of fresh leafy and fruited vegetables, beansprouts and mushrooms; and 30% of our local consumption of eggs and seafood.

key_points.point: Meats are excluded from the revised targets due to resource efficiency, land intensity and climate conditions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Protein types such as meats are not part of the revised targets due to factors such as resource efficiency, land intensity and climate conditions.

key_points.point: Alternative protein is excluded because the sector is nascent.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Alternative protein is also excluded given the nascency of the sector.

key_points.point: Rice and poultry will be considered under other pillars such as import diversification and stockpiling.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: What we are not intending to produce locally, such as rice and poultry, will be considered under other pillars of the Singapore Food Story 2 such as import diversification and stockpiling.

key_points.point: Support for farms includes lowering production costs, building capability, strengthening input supply resilience and enhancing demand offtake.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: To achieve them, we will continue to find ways to support new and existing farms in lowering production costs, building capability, strengthening the supply resilience of inputs and enhancing demand offtake.

key_points.point: Current local production is about 26% of the 30% protein target and 8% of the 20% leafy vegetable target.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: We have about 26% out of 30%. We have about 8% out of 20% for the leafy vegetables

key_points.point: Between 2019 and 2024, farm yields increased by 10% for vegetables, 17% for seafood and 50% for eggs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: the productivity of farms has increased in yield by 10% for vegetables, 17% for seafood and 50% for eggs.

key_points.point: The Ministry goes with free market principles rather than minimum local sourcing requirements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: we go with free market principles

left_open: A direct comparison of the revised targets with the '30 by 30' targets in terms of total local food production volume.
A specific measure of Singapore's food security relative to local farming production.
A detailed assessment of how the revised targets will remain adequate, sustainable and resilient to current and future challenges.
Concrete job creation or retention targets accompanying the new production goals.
Assessment of potential price impacts on households and measures to prevent local production from raising food prices.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered support for farms, job and price impacts, food security measurement, diversification, and minimum local sourcing.
